description:
Surfaced from bd:JMAP-mno4.12 (review of crate-jmap-jscalendar-types). All workspace type crates currently use std::collections::HashMap<K, V> on public wire types (jmap-types, jmap-mail-types, jmap-chat-types, jmap-jscalendar-types, jmap-jscontact-types). serde_json's Serialize for HashMap iterates in RandomState order → byte output of any struct containing a HashMap with ≥2 entries is non-deterministic.

This is a workspace-wide question, not a per-crate question. Possible workspace answers:

1. **Keep HashMap** (status quo). Document the non-determinism as a known property; consumers who need byte-stable output normalize externally. Lowest-blast-radius, but the determinism gap stays.

2. **Switch all to BTreeMap**. Deterministic lexicographic order. Adds Ord bound on key types (most are String which already has Ord; LocalDateTime/Id would need PartialOrd+Ord derive — non-breaking additions). Breaking the field-type contract but workspace is pre-1.0 and all relevant structs are #[non_exhaustive].

3. **Switch all to indexmap::IndexMap**. Insertion-order preserved. Requires adding indexmap dep — currently forbidden by the per-crate AGENTS.md restrictions (jscalendar-types limits deps to jmap-types/serde/serde_json). Would need workspace-policy revision.

Recommendation: option 2 (BTreeMap). Reasons: (a) determinism is the workspace default per RustCrypto-stance and reproducible-build concerns; (b) the canonical-template consistency rule means doing it crate-by-crate is wrong, the sweep should land workspace-wide in one pass; (c) key types in scope are all String or simple newtypes-around-String, so the Ord bound is free; (d) #[non_exhaustive] + pre-1.0 means the API-break is acceptable; (e) avoids adding indexmap dep across 7+ crates.

Scope-of-sweep: would cover jmap-types::wire, jmap-types::methods, jmap-mail-types::email/mdn/submission, jmap-chat-types::message, jmap-jscalendar-types (this crate), jmap-jscontact-types if any. Per-crate child beads under this epic.

Test discipline: each crate adds a deterministic-serialization test (≥2-entry map serializes to lexicographically-sorted JSON).

Filing as 'human' because workspace-architectural posture decisions require human judgment per workspace AGENTS.md — see 'When NOT to file human' policy, this does NOT fall into any of the four anti-patterns: not frontier-cycling, not deferred+human, no stale committed recommendation, work has not been done. The recommendation above is provided so the human can ratify quickly if they agree.
title: Workspace-architectural: HashMap vs BTreeMap on JMAP wire types
